source_text: Pro condicione mortalis corporis incurrunt et aegritudinum aerumnas et dolorum poenas et pericula morborum. Non solum ergo parvulis necessariam Christi, a quo et facti sunt, medicinam fatemur, sed etiam omnium mortalium naturae.
pass_a_gloss: For the condition of a mortal body they incur both the toils of illnesses and the punishments of pains and the dangers of diseases. Not only therefore do we confess the medicine of Christ, by whom they have also been made, necessary to little ones, but also to the nature of all mortals.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis
LS medicina; Blaise of Christ as physician

pass_b_english: Because their bodies are mortal, they also encounter the hardships of illness, the suffering of pain, and the dangers of disease. We therefore acknowledge Christ’s medicine as necessary not only to infants, whom he also made, but to the nature of all mortals.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
